A 12.46-carat diamond ring led Doyle's Important Jewelry sale at $457,700, but the widest margin over estimate belonged to a pair of 1890 sapphire earrings.

The sapphire pair made $140,200 against a $30,000 to $50,000 estimate, 2.80 times the high and the biggest beat of the sale's top five lots. Four of five topped their books; the one that didn't, a Tiffany Fleurage bracelet, was already priced in six figures.

Origin and treatment aren't published on the sapphires, so this desk can't call Kashmir or unheated. What's certain is the price: $17,160 a carat before the mount.

Gold was re-read at $4,622.30 an ounce this morning, down $11.90, while silver clawed back nearly all of yesterday's loss.

Kitco and TradingEconomics agreed within $1.54 on gold and 13 cents on silver. Gold is down $21.60 or 0.465% across two sessions, from Monday's $4,643.90. Silver rose 0.99% on yesterday, narrowing the gold-to-silver ratio to 67.43 from 68.27. Platinum and palladium both held a sixth session at $1,881.00 and $1,336.00.

Two down days after a run is a pause. This morning's real number is the width: a $59.10 range by 6am, more than most benches mark up a finished piece.
